title: Review loop 3: full project sweep
notes:
kith-attach/kithctl review: 10% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) did not exercise write_blob_streaming against a chunked HTTP body with multiple frames to verify per-chunk size accounting is correct in all frame orderings; (2) did not inspect rusqlite::backup::Backup::new failure modes in practice to confirm stub-file cleanup is truly required; (3) watch.rs reconnect logic not traced against all kithd response codes.
kith-tui review: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) whether the stateMismatch recovery path is reachable in practice and whether the message_state set from sc.new_state vs. actual server state creates a window for missed messages — I traced it as safe but the logic is subtle; (2) whether the 500-message limit combined with the position:0 query means the truncation notice compares the wrong segment (it does: it shows newest 500, hides oldest, which is correct); (3) SSE stream splitting behavior on chunk boundaries is not exercised by tests — the run_sse buf accumulation could theoretically split a blank-line boundary across two chunks.
kith-store review: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) I did not trace every call site that calls update_last_message_at/set_blocked/upsert to confirm whether callers compensate for the non-atomic two-phase write with their own locking; if kithd holds a higher-level Mutex around all store operations the crash window is real but the race window is not. (2) I did not read kith-chat or kithd to see how get_changes_since_for_chat is called or whether callers already hold state together. (3) SQLite query plan selection was inferred from index availability, not verified with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.
kith-jmap/kith-peer review: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) did not trace kith-chat and kithd crates to verify outbox_worker spawn site panic handling, (2) did not verify whether kith-store's insert_message_with_attachments is actually transactional end-to-end (assumed from surrounding code), (3) RFC 8620 createdIds issue may already be handled at the kith-chat layer — cannot confirm without reading those handlers, (4) group-chat Peer/deliver fallthrough: if chatId is unknown and contact has a group-only history (no direct chat), case (c) creates a direct chat with contact_id=sender — this may be correct per spec but worth verifying against architecture doc.
core/events/tslocal review: 10% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) I could not run the code or cargo check it, so I cannot rule out a subtle type mismatch at a call site. (2) The Argument<T> untagged deserialization interaction with the kith-jmap resolver is analyzed from the resultref.rs source alone without reading the full dispatcher (kith-jmap/src/lib.rs); the dispatcher may have compensating logic that fully neutralizes the risk. (3) I did not trace every call site of peer_nodes_excluding to verify whether the caller has a fallback for the wrong-node case. (4) The UserProfile.display_name empty-string case from Tailscale Inc. vs Headscale was inferred from comments, not from Tailscale API documentation.
kith-chat review: 15% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty: (1) did not read kith-store message.rs get_querychanges_since_for_chat in full - possible off-by-one in position index computation for Message/queryChanges added entries; (2) did not verify that Contact/queryChanges correctly handles the case where a contact is both removed-from-query and added-to-query in the same delta (contacts can't be destroyed so removed is always empty, making this moot); (3) did not confirm whether ChatContactChangesHandler's 'Phase 1 contacts only produce added' comment was ever correct - the store has always advanced changed_at_counter on updates.
kithd review (kithd crate, this session): ~85% chance of no missed P0 correctness bug beyond the two filed (build_dispatcher arity, mailbox_host provenance). Uncertainty: (1) did not trace every store mutation in kith-store to verify atomicity claims made in prior review — those P0s may have siblings in kithd handlers; (2) peer_fetch.rs fragile string-match on 'length limit' could mask size-enforcement failures under a library update but the check itself is present; (3) TailnetCertVerifier accepts any tailnet IP cert without hostname binding — the security argument is sound but was not independently verified against the Tailscale WireGuard model; (4) did not inspect kith-attach BlobStore for TOCTOU on the filesystem path after blobId validation. No material gaps in auth.rs, static_files.rs, events.rs, or the main router ordering.
